definitions.explanation: The older, more complex forms of kanji that were in standard use before the postwar script reform of 1946. These were replaced by simplified {新字体|しんじたい} (new-form kanji) for everyday use.

examples.english: 國 is the old-form kanji for 国.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{本|ほん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{旧字体|きゅうじたい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{使|つか}われている→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。

⟦{人名|じんめい}→人名：22206_jinmei⟧や⟦{地名|ちめい}→地名：04059_chimei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{旧字体|きゅうじたい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{使|つか}われる→使う：00473_tsukau⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Old-form kanji are still sometimes used in personal names and place names.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{旧|きゅう}→旧：19346_kyuu⟧ (old, former), ⟦{字|じ}→字：01606_ji⟧ (character), and ⟦{体|たい}→体：09872_tai⟧ (form, style). The simplification of kanji was part of Japan's postwar education reforms in 1946, when the {当用漢字|とうようかんじ} (characters for everyday use) list was established. Examples include {學|がく}→⟦{学|がく}→〜学：09846_gaku⟧, {國|くに}→⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧, {會|かい}→⟦{会|あ}う→会う：00482_au⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旧字体|きゅうじたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧ — to write in old-form kanji
- {旧字体|きゅうじたい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{新字体|しんじたい}→新字体：27162_shinjitai⟧ — old-form and new-form kanji
- {旧字体|きゅうじたい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{漢字|かんじ}→漢字：09480_kanji⟧ — old-form kanji characters
